course_description:
This course provides pedagogical content knowledge and curriculum knowledge for prospective primary school teachers in relation to the Australian Curriculum: Science. A variety of contexts are used to explore a range of appropriate teaching models and authentic assessment techniques in line with current approaches to teaching in the primary school. There is emphasis on the integration of technologies including ICT into teaching practice as well as integration of topics across the three interrelated strands.

The course builds on the content knowledge previously developed. It focuses on developing your pedagogical content knowledge, understanding key classroom strategies and allowing time for you to practice your craft. Science Inquiry and Science as a Human Endeavour form the foundation of the course in recognition of the contribution of both people and other disciplines in developing understandings.

course_aims: The course will develop students' knowledge and skills and their application to teaching science in the Queensland primary school setting. Students will engage with current and emerging research-based approaches to teaching science, focusing on practical issues in the classroom and developing ideas about learning and its facilitation. The course will take a contextual approach in which beginning teachers develop the skills to draw out science in various classroom settings.

learning_outcomes.description: Analyse science topics, identifying appropriate levels of conceptual development and contexts for teaching the topics in the primary years of schooling.
Use science education literature to inform your teaching practice.
Collaboratively develop resources including activities, laboratory experiments and units of work for teaching using a variety of pedagogical approaches focusing on inquiry learning.
Develop students scientific literacy and ability to participate in scientific thinking in social and technological contexts.
Create pieces of assessment for diagnostic, formative and summative assessment in the science classroom that align with the Australian Curriculum.
Discuss current issues related to assessment of student work in science.

Work effectively and collaboratively in teams to make informed team decisions, demonstrate interpersonal, leadership and communication skills, and critically evaluate personal and peer contributions to team processes.

assessment_details.title: Evaluating an Inquiry Unit of Work
assessment_details.task_description: A unit plan organises curriculum content into a coherent sequence for learning and teaching over a set period of time (e.g., a term). In Primary Science, the resources we select should support this coherence by meaningfully supporting student engagement and understanding. In this task, you will analyse an existing unit of work using a CoRe Matrix and evaluate it against the Australian Curriculum: Science V9 through the lens of Constructive Alignment, which focuses on the coherence between learning outcomes, teaching strategies, and assessment. The task consists of two parts. Part 1 – Analysis (approx. 1000 words) Critique a Primary Connections unit of work and use this analysis to develop a CoRe Matrix for the three phases of the unit (Launch, Inquire, Act). The CoRe matrix provides a holistic representation of a sequential unit of work. It helps identify students’ prior knowledge, potential misconceptions, and effective teaching strategies and assessment approaches that promote student learning. [The Matrix template will be provided and modelled in class.] Building on your critique and through your CoRe matrix, demonstrate a clear understanding of the unit’s conceptual focus and pedagogical intent. This includes articulating an Essential Question for the unit and outlining the background knowledge necessary for effective teaching. Any text taken directly from the Primary Connections resource must be written in italics and appropriately referenced. Part 2 – Evaluation (approx. 1000 words) In this section, you will extend your analysis by evaluating the unit through the lens of Constructive Alignment. Your task is to consider both how well the unit aligns learning outcomes, teaching strategies, and assessment, and why this alignment is essential for designing meaningful Primary Science learning. Your discussion should focus on the significance of alignment for coherent planning: how clear intentions guide purposeful teaching, how aligned learning experiences support conceptual development, and how assessment provides meaningful evidence of learning. You should also reflect on what engaging with Constructive Alignment reveals about your own developing practice and how it shapes your approach to designing intentional, responsive science learning. assessment_details.title: Plan a Sequence of Learning about a Science Phenomenon
assessment_details.task_description: A phenomenon is simply an observable event that can be explained scientifically. In the science classroom, a carefully chosen phenomenon can drive student inquiry. Phenomena add relevance to the science classroom, showing students science in their own world. A good phenomenon is observable, interesting, complex, and aligned to the appropriate curriculum standard. In a group of three (3), choose a science phenomenon as the focus for your planning: Identify, describe and explain the science behind your phenomenon and its role in the science classroom. [Images may be used]. A synopsis of background scientific information helps teachers deepen their understanding of the science they are required to teach. This should answer the question: As the teacher, what science content do I need to know? (approx. 600 words) Using the identified phenomenon as a starting point, write a sequence of 3 inquiry-based lessons (Launch, Inquire, Act) to support inclusive participation and engagement in the inquiry process. Risk assessment/s and specifics about the classroom environment must be included. Each lesson plan must be attributed to an individual. (approx. 2400 words) A note about group work: You will receive a single group mark for this task, as all group members should contribute equally to the design and delivery of the assessment task. However, exceptions can be made in the event of one or more group members engaging in ‘social loafing’ (also known as ‘free-riding’): Free riding is a form of social loafing observed in groups when one or more members slack off and ‘ride’ on the extra efforts of their co-workers (Walker & Angelo, 1998). If your small group is experiencing dysfunction, including ‘social loafing’ by one or more members, it is your responsibility to bring this promptly to the attention of your tutor/course coordinator, who will then support the group to resolve the problems in a respectful way. If no resolution can be found, the tutor/course coordinator can take steps, including removing the non-contributing student(s) from the group and requiring the student(s) to complete the task either individually or in another small group with other ‘social loafers’. assessment_details.title: Teaching a Science Concept: Part 1
assessment_details.task_description: Working in your groups, you will collaboratively design and deliver a 30-minute LIA (Launch-Inquire-Act) micro-teaching episode that teaches a science concept based on your identified phenomenon. Your presentation should model inquiry-based science teaching and demonstrate how the phenomenon can be used as an anchor for conceptual development. Your presentation must: Introduce the lesson segment by briefly explaining where your phase fits within the full LIA sequence and how the task(s) in your segment backmap to the intended summative assessment. Teach your allocated phase of the lesson, demonstrating clear pedagogical intent, accurate science content, and strategies that support inclusive participation and engagement. Use a range of verbal and non‑verbal communication strategies to enhance clarity, support inquiry, and promote student understanding. Address safety and classroom environment considerations, including any required risk assessments relevant to your phase. Respond to questions without notice from peers and your tutor, demonstrating your understanding of the science concept, the inquiry process, and your pedagogical choices. The focus of this task is on developing Pedagogical Content Knowledge, modelling inquiry through the LIA structure, and demonstrating how direct teaching can be used purposefully within an inquiry‑based approach. The micro-teaching episode will be video-recorded for your reflection (Assessment task 4B) and will occur during class time (lectures or tutorials) in Week 13. APST: 1.2, 2.2, 3.1, 3.3, 3.4, 3.5 Read full task description Hide full task description

assessment_details.task_description: After your teaching event, you will receive specific feedback from several of your peers. You will also have access to the video recording of your presentation. Write an individual critical reflection on your mini‑lesson, supported by relevant literature. Your reflection should: review your own teaching, acknowledge how collaboration with peers (including classroom discussion) contributed to your learning critically examine the strengths and tensions of inquiry‑based learning consider how this professional learning experience informs your development toward becoming a highly proficient science teacher. learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 1 To Week 3 (27 Jul - 16 Aug)
learning_activities.topic: Teaching Science The introductory module will provide an overview of the importance and challenges of teaching science to primary-age students in an increasingly STEM-oriented world. Models of curriculum, pedagogy and assessment will be explored in advance of first-hand experience in schools. Tutorials will focus on practical activities designed to engage and motivate young students across the sub-strands of Science Understanding. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L04, L05, L06

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 4 To Week 8 (17 Aug - 20 Sep)
learning_activities.topic: Break due to professional experience placement No classes scheduled while undertaking professional experience (placement) in an accompanying course.

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 9 To Week 10 (21 Sep - 11 Oct)
learning_activities.topic: Planning for Teaching Science After seeing science teaching in the classroom, students will examine critical aspects of planning using science content knowledge and pedagogical content knowledge in order to develop their identity as science teachers. Tutorials will explore the sub-strands of the Science Understanding strand to incorporate content and strategies that promote meaningful and valued learning. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07

learning_activities.learning_period: Multiple weeks From Week 11 To Week 13 (12 Oct - 01 Nov)
learning_activities.topic: Preparing to Teach Science Lectures will continue to focus on developing the pedagogical content knowledge and curriculum connections required in teaching science to students in the primary years. Tutorials will allow students to develop their pedagogical skills by practising teaching and evaluating a short lesson around a particular concept. This module also includes opportunity for students to practice through micro-teaching. Learning outcomes: L01, L02, L03, L04, L05, L06, L07
